en: The Apadāna of the Elder Ekacampakapupphiya Mandāravapupphiya Chapter 8, Number 8 [He] offered a single campaka flower to the Buddha, the Teacher, who was seated upon his throne. Because of that deed, he was reborn in the realm of the Thirty-three gods, where he enjoyed celestial pleasures for ten thousand aeons. having taken a single campaka flower,”
I approached the supreme among men,
the unsurpassed Pacceka-muni, with a clear heart and a joyful mind.
Taking it up with both hands,
Because I offered that flower in worship,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Ekacampakapupphiya spoke these verses.
This is the eighth legend of the elder Ekacampakapupphiya.
